what: The boss parsons explanation states a wrong fact about matching: it says the one-word and multi-word shapes can go in either order 'so their order doesn't change the result', and names a pattern `["hi", name]` that isn't in the program. The real second case is `["hi", *names]`, which also fits `["hi"]` (star captures zero items), so swapping the two cases changes the output.
evidence: b3m explain: "A one-word [\"hi\"] and a two-word [\"hi\", name] are different shapes, so their order doesn't change the result, but _ must be last." boss_parsons.py lines 3-6: case ["hi"]: ... case ["hi", *names]:. Scratch run on CPython 3.15.2 with the two cases swapped prints "Hello, ! Hello, Ada and Bo!" instead of the goal "Hello! Hello, Ada and Bo!". The chapter's own map (panel 28, drop road) says "The starred capture always makes a list, even of zero or one item."
fix: Rewrite the explain: "The labelled def comes first, then match cmd:. [\"hi\"] must come before [\"hi\", *names], because *names can also be empty, so the starred case would grab a lone \"hi\" and print 'Hello, !'. _ is last. The last line calls it twice."

what: The parsons key is ambiguous. Moving the `__init__` pair under Dog and the `speak` pair under Pet gives a valid program with the same goal output, but the engine checks exact line order and marks it wrong.
evidence: boss_parsons.py: class Pet / def __init__ / self.name = name / class Dog(Pet) / def speak / return ... / rex = Dog("rex") / print(rex.speak()). A scratch run of the swapped version (Pet gets speak, Dog gets __init__) on 3.15.2 prints "Rex says woof", the same as the goal. assets/comic-widgets.js:487 grades by `mine === real` (exact order). Prompt: "Rebuild the parent, the child, and the two lines that use them."
fix: Say the split in the prompt: "Pet sets the name in __init__; Dog adds speak." Or change the program so only one split works (e.g. give Dog's speak a dog-only word, and give Pet a second method that Dog uses).
